banana peel.disposal_method: Put in the green/wet-waste bin. Best composted at home or via community compost pits.
banana peel.eco_tip: Fruit and vegetable peels make excellent compost and reduce methane emissions from landfills.

vegetable peels.disposal_method: Green/wet-waste bin or home compost bin.
vegetable peels.eco_tip: Composting kitchen waste can cut your household landfill contribution by up to 30%.

food leftovers.disposal_method: Green/wet-waste bin. Avoid mixing with plastic wrappers.
food leftovers.eco_tip: Plan meals to reduce food waste at the source — the most sustainable option.

tea bags.eco_tip: Used tea leaves also work as a natural plant fertilizer.

garden waste.eco_tip: Leaves and twigs decompose quickly and enrich soil quality.

newspaper.disposal_method: Blue/dry-waste bin. Keep dry and bundled for recyclers.
newspaper.eco_tip: Recycling paper saves trees, water, and energy compared to making new paper.

cardboard box.disposal_method: Flatten and place in the blue/dry-waste bin.
cardboard box.eco_tip: Flattening boxes saves collection space and transport fuel.

plastic bottle.disposal_method: Rinse, remove cap, and place in the blue/dry-waste bin.
plastic bottle.eco_tip: A rinsed bottle is far more likely to actually get recycled than a dirty one.

glass bottle.disposal_method: Rinse and place in the blue/dry-waste bin; handle carefully if broken.
glass bottle.eco_tip: Glass can be recycled endlessly without losing quality.

aluminium can.disposal_method: Rinse and place in the blue/dry-waste bin.
aluminium can.eco_tip: Recycling aluminium uses up to 95% less energy than producing it from raw ore.

metal scrap.disposal_method: Blue/dry-waste bin or a local scrap dealer.
metal scrap.eco_tip: Scrap metal has real resale value — consider a scrap collection drive.

plastic wrapper.disposal_method: Blue/dry-waste bin if clean; many municipalities also accept multilayer wrappers at collection drives.
plastic wrapper.eco_tip: Reducing single-use wrapper purchases helps more than recycling them.

old clothes.disposal_method: Donate if usable; otherwise take to a textile-recycling drop-off point.
old clothes.eco_tip: Textile waste is a major landfill contributor — donation extends a garment's life.

battery.disposal_method: Do NOT put in regular bins. Drop off at a designated e-waste/battery collection point.
battery.eco_tip: Batteries contain heavy metals that can contaminate soil and groundwater.

medicine.disposal_method: Return expired medicines to a pharmacy take-back program; do not flush.
medicine.eco_tip: Flushed medicines can pollute water systems and harm aquatic life.

paint can.disposal_method: Take to a hazardous-waste collection facility; never pour down a drain.
paint can.eco_tip: Leftover paint can be donated to community art or repair projects.

cfl bulb.disposal_method: Drop off at an e-waste or CFL collection point; do not break or bin normally.
cfl bulb.eco_tip: CFL bulbs contain trace mercury and need specialized recycling.

syringe.disposal_method: Return to a pharmacy or clinic for safe biomedical disposal. Never place in household bins.
syringe.eco_tip: Biomedical waste needs specialized handling to prevent injury and infection spread.

mobile phone.disposal_method: Drop off at an authorized e-waste collection center or manufacturer take-back program.
mobile phone.eco_tip: E-waste contains recoverable gold, copper, and rare earth elements.

laptop.disposal_method: Authorized e-waste recycler; wipe personal data first.
laptop.eco_tip: Refurbishing or donating working electronics extends their useful life.

charger cable.disposal_method: E-waste collection point, not the regular dustbin.
charger cable.eco_tip: Cables contain recyclable copper — never burn e-waste to extract metals.

thermocol.disposal_method: Dry-waste bin, but check local rules — some cities ban thermocol entirely.
thermocol.eco_tip: Try switching to compostable or reusable packaging alternatives.

sanitary waste.disposal_method: Wrap securely and place in a marked red 'sanitary waste' bin, separate from wet/dry waste.
sanitary waste.eco_tip: Never flush sanitary items — they clog pipes and pollute waterways.
